title: Al-Masad: the palm-fiber rope
hook: a warning about Abu Lahab, the Prophet's own uncle and enemy (Surah 111)

segments.voice: Yesterday: al-Ikhlas, worth a third of the Qur'an. Your line was short, and heavy. Did you say one short thing slowly, and did it weigh more than usual? Day one hundred sixty-three.

Every family has someone. The uncle who turns every holiday dinner into an argument. The cousin who takes your news and makes it about himself. Most of the time it's small. For the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ it was not small. His uncle, his father's own brother, became one of his fiercest public enemies. And the Qur'an names him. Only one of the Prophet's opponents in Mecca is named in the Qur'an, and it's this man, family. Today: Al-Masad, the palm-fiber rope.
screen: `EVERY FAMILY HAS SOMEONE.` → `HIS OWN UNCLE.` → `THE ONLY ENEMY NAMED.`

segments.voice: The story is in Sahih al-Bukhari. When the Prophet was told to warn his own clan, he climbed the hill of Safa in Mecca and called out to the families of Quraysh, one by one, until they gathered. He asked: if I told you an army was behind this hill, would you believe me? They said: we've never known you to lie. Then, he said, I am a warner to you before a severe punishment. And his uncle, Abu Lahab, answered: may you perish! Is this what you gathered us for? The surah answers him, with his own word. Pickthall translates the first line: The power of Abu Lahab will perish, and he will perish. Abu Lahab wasn't his real name. It means father of flame, a nickname, some say for his glowing, ruddy face. The surah says his wealth and his gains won't help him. It names his wife too, who, commentators say, scattered thorns in the Prophet's path: she'll carry firewood, with a rope of palm fiber, masad, around her neck. The surah is named for that rope. Here's what scholars point out. The Prophet's family didn't protect Abu Lahab. Being the Prophet's uncle, the closest possible tie, was not a guarantee of anything. And the reverse is true in the same story: another uncle, Abu Talib, protected the Prophet for years. Two brothers, the same nephew, two different choices. Kin is not a guarantee. Not of harm, not of goodness. What counts, in the Qur'an's telling, is what each person does.
screen: `A CALL FROM THE HILL OF SAFA.` · `MAY YOU PERISH — HIS UNCLE'S ANSWER.` · `A ROPE OF PALM FIBER.` · `TWO UNCLES, TWO CHOICES.` · then, large: `KIN IS NOT A GUARANTEE.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice. Sit, and think of your family, the one you were born into or the one you've made. Notice one person whose closeness to you has been a gift, and one relationship where being related hasn't made things good. Don't judge either one. Just hold both as true. Then turn it around, gently: being part of your family isn't a guarantee for you either. What would you want your own choices to add? The bell holds the time.
Al-Masad. The palm-fiber rope, the name of Surah one hundred eleven, about the Prophet's uncle Abu Lahab. Today's word.
Your line: kin is not a guarantee. Today, notice when you assume someone is good, or bad, because of who they belong to. Look at what they do instead. Day one hundred sixty-three.

howItsDone: Surah al-Masad, also called al-Lahab, is recited in the prayers like other short surahs; Muslims learn its story, the Prophet's call from Safa and his uncle's reply, as part of the life of the Prophet.

original.note: Arabic: twisted fiber, a rope of palm fiber; the last word of Surah 111.

trapdoor: what you thought: a curse on an old enemy.
what it means: a warning that even the Prophet's own uncle wasn't protected by kinship; each is judged by what he does.
what a scholar hears: the surah answers Abu Lahab's tabban ('may you perish') with tabbat; Bukhari 4971 gives the Safa scene; he is the only Meccan opponent named in the Qur'an.

notes: Please confirm the exact Pickthall wording of 111:1.
The wife (Umm Jamil) scattering thorns is from the commentaries; the script says 'commentators say'. Some commentators read 'carrier of firewood' as a figure for spreading slander.
The nickname explanation (ruddy face) is one traditional explanation; hedged with 'some say'.
'Only opponent named' is widely stated; confirm.
